answer: Commit-reveal with seeded words forces each agent to hash a promise before the challenge arrives. When the network publishes "walnut, opal, copper," every agent reveals its precommitted answer embedding those exact terms. An attacker spawning a thousand identities cannot precompute responses or share one good answer across clones, because the seed changes per round. Each fake identity must perform the full inference, multiplying compute cost linearly with sybil count and making mass impersonation prohibitively expensive.
